ety.text: Derived from Sauraseni Prakrit मच्छ (maccha) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀮- (-la-) + -𑀇𑀓𑀸- (-ikā-), from Ashokan Prakrit 𑀫𑀙 (macha /⁠maccha⁠/) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀮- (-la-) + -𑀇𑀓𑀸- (-ikā-), from Sanskrit मत्स्य (mátsya). Cognate with Awadhi मछरी (machrī), Gujarati માછલી (māchlī), Konkani मासोळी (māsoḷī), Magadhi Prakrit 𑀫𑀰𑁆𑀘𑀮𑀻 (maścalī). This -𑀮- (-la-) extended form appears to have spread from Eastern Hindi.

Inherited from Prakrit लड्डुअ (laḍḍua) without cluster simplification—compare Punjabi ਲੱਡੂ (laḍḍū)—, from Sanskrit लड्डुक (laḍḍuka), from लड्डु (laḍḍu, “a kind of sweetmeat”). Compare लाड़ू (lāṛū), लड़ुआ (laṛuā). Cognate with Gujarati લાડવો (lāḍvo), લાડુ (lāḍu), Marathi लाडू (lāḍū), Odia ଲଡୁ (laḍu), Bengali লাড্ডু (laḍḍu) / নাড়ু (naṛu), Sinhalese ලඩු (laḍu).
Borrowed from Classical Persian شترمرغ (šuturmurġ). Analyzable as शुतुर (śutur, “camel”) + मुर्ग़ (murġ, “fowl”).
